description: codebase-kg hooks. (1) A PreToolUse search gate on Grep, Glob, Bash and PowerShell, which calls the codebase-kg server directly (type mcp_tool, tool kg_hook_search_gate) and starts no process: a Grep/Glob (or shell grep/rg/git grep/find) of a directory that holds mapped code is denied with the instruction to query the code graph first. A graph query clears the next gate_credit searches; the server counts the queries itself, per session, and a server restart resets the count. A search that names its files, one aimed outside the code the graph maps, one that can only match non-source files (plists, images, Xcode project files), and a repeat of a denied search (the same pattern, however reworded) are all free. Inside a subagent the gate adds the instruction as context instead of denying. When the server is unreachable the search is allowed. (2) A PostToolUse commit check on Bash and PowerShell `git *` commands, which calls the codebase-kg server directly (type mcp_tool, tool kg_hook_commit_check) and starts no process: after a command that made a commit, the server lists the committed source no node covers, the deleted source the graph still anchors on and the mapped source that changed since the graph was updated, as context for the agent, with the instruction to run /codebase-kg:refresh and commit the graph in a follow-up commit before pushing. It is advisory, never blocks, and says nothing when the server is unreachable. Both honor .claude/codebase-kg.local.md (search_gate, gate_credit, gate_shell_search, commit_check, root, graph_path), and both no-op when the repo has no graph. SKIP_KG does not apply to either hook: search_gate: off in the per-clone file turns the gate off. (3) A PreToolUse push gate on Bash and PowerShell `git *` commands, which calls the codebase-kg server directly (tool kg_hook_push_gate): a `git push` (also `git -C <dir> push`, chained or env-prefixed) is denied while any mapped file is stale against HEAD, with the instruction to run /codebase-kg:refresh, commit the graph and push again without asking the user. An agent cannot skip the check on its own: a push prefixed with SKIP_KG=1 or a matching KG_STALE_ACK=<n> makes the server ask the user, through an MCP elicitation that lists the stale files, or through the permission prompt in a client without elicitation, and a run with no user is refused. --no-verify does not skip it. A second PreToolUse hook on the six graph write tools answers allow (tool kg_hook_allow_write), so a refresh does not stop at a permission prompt. Both fail open when the server is unreachable; the git pre-push hook still blocks. (4) A SessionStart notice: a repo that committed the vendored checkers but whose clone has no core.hooksPath or diff.codegraph.textconv gets one line naming the install command, and a clone whose graph diff driver names a missing plugin folder gets one line naming /codebase-kg:setup. It never wires a clone — git leaves .git/config out of a clone so that cloning cannot cause code to run, and wiring it automatically would route around that. In a wired clone whose diff driver pins an older codebase-kg release, it moves the pin to the installed release once that tag is published, and prints one line. (5) A SessionStart server start: when nothing answers GET /health on the server_port setting, or an older codebase-kg build does, it starts this build's shared server detached and waits up to 8 s; it prints one line only when the port belongs to another program or the server does not come up. (6) The SessionStart server start also registers the session with the agent's process id. The server drops a session whose process has exited, so no SessionEnd hook is needed: a server that has seen a registered session exits after CODEBASE_KG_SESSION_GRACE seconds (default 300) with none live and no use.
